note: Adapted from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original describes only the soldier, records the alate as Not known and does not describe the worker. The headline is OCR'd as "Hamitermes (Hamitermes) c olonu& sp. nov." and the caption as "Hamitermes Colonus"; "Pig." is an error for Fig.; "sth" is an error for 5th. The type locality, New South Wales: Griffith, agrees with the checklist. Distribution and biology have not been translated into the morphology sections.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The position and shape of the mandibular teeth resemble those of A. dentosus, but the two species differ considerably in body colour and head shape; this is a very distinctive species with no close relatives.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Not recorded in the original (Not known).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Medium-sized species; mandibles rather long and slightly curved; mandibular teeth short, triangular, situated near the base of the mandible. Head pale yellow to orange-yellow; labrum and antennae orange-yellow; mandibles rust-coloured, orange-yellow at the base. Head oval, widest at the middle, with very few hairs. Mandibles slightly shorter than the head capsule; teeth almost on the same line as the apex of the labrum. Basal half of the labrum with the sides nearly parallel, distal half narrowing to a blunt apex. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 3 very small; segment 4 only slightly longer than segment 5; segment 6 longer than segments 4 and 5. Measurements: total length 5.15—5.25 mm, head length (including mandibles) 2.20—2.34 mm, head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.17—1.28 mm, head length (to apex of labrum) 1.65—1.72 mm, head width 1.10—1.15 mm, pronotum length 0.34—0.38 mm, width 0.67—0.69 mm.
